title: Extraction & Ingestion Quality
description: Study chunking for relation extraction, schema-constrained extraction, confidence and human review, and incremental updates and deletion. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Chunking for relation extraction
lessons.description: Choose context windows and a duplicate-assertion key.
lessons.conceptOverview: Chunks must retain enough context to identify relation subjects and qualifiers. Overlap can help continuity but creates duplicate assertions, so deduplicate using source identity and normalized claims.
lessons.whyItMatters: Extraction needs contextual continuity and deduplication.

lessons.title: Schema-constrained extraction
lessons.description: Define structural and evidence validation as separate gates.
lessons.conceptOverview: Constrain output types and validate relation endpoints against the schema. Structural validity does not establish truth; follow it with evidence checks and rejection of unsupported assertions.
lessons.whyItMatters: Schema compliance and factual support require separate checks.

lessons.title: Confidence and human review
lessons.description: Design a review policy based on uncertainty and consequence.
lessons.conceptOverview: Confidence estimates should be calibrated against labeled examples if used for automated acceptance. Review high-impact or ambiguous assertions even when a model reports confidence, and track reviewer corrections.
lessons.whyItMatters: Self-reported confidence is not a substitute for measured reliability.

lessons.title: Incremental updates and deletion
lessons.description: Map source-to-assertion dependencies and write a deletion verification plan.
lessons.conceptOverview: Track which graph artifacts depend on each source so updates and deletions propagate to assertions, summaries and indexes. Rebuilding only a text chunk can leave stale derived relationships.
lessons.whyItMatters: Deletion must propagate through derived graph artifacts.
